prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-05-08. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 12.41 |
| Retained earnings       | 45,912M |
| Current liabilities     | 15,003M |
| Current assets          | 186,246M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 49,234M |
| Total liabilities       | 444,085M |
| Total assets            | 493,319M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,188M |
| Revenue                 | 7,300M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-05-08, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a very strong current ratio (12.41) indicating excellent short-term liquidity. However, the debt-to-equity ratio is extremely high at 9.02x (444,085M / 49,234M), and the debt-to-asset ratio is also concerning at 0.90 (444,085M / 493,319M), suggesting a heavily leveraged capital structure. The EBIT to revenue margin is low at 43.67% (3,188M / 7,300M), indicating weak operating profitability relative to sales.

DECISION: B+
